name: SVTronics, Inc
old_description: SVTronics offers fully integrated solutions to customers who require more than just a PCB assembly. Our MAG team specializes in delivering fully integrated solutions with highly diversified requirements.
about:
SVTronics, Inc. operates from its headquarters in Plano, Texas. The company holds Minority Business Certification, a HUBZone certificate, and a Small Business Enterprise certificate, reflecting its minority-owned, small-business status. Leadership includes Zenon “Bud” Maciekowicz, who directs the Military Aerospace and Government business unit.

The firm provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing, ranging from prototype to high-volume production. Its facility runs a fully automated high-speed SMT line alongside a dedicated prototype SMT line, with placement capability down to 01005 components. Processes include screen printing with automated vision, wave and selective soldering for through-hole parts, conformal coating, mechanical assembly, cable and wire harness fabrication, and system integration and testing. Engineering services cover mechanical and electrical design, new product introduction, and DFM/DFA analysis.

SVTronics serves the military, aerospace, and government sectors through its MAG business unit, and its ISO 13485 certification indicates capability for medical device work. Customers include defense primes and government agencies requiring ITAR-compliant production.

The company emphasizes domestic manufacturing, promoting an online quoting tool that accepts Gerber and ODB++ files, automatically sources bill-of-materials parts, and delivers instant DFM/DFA reports. It positions itself as a partner for restoring U.S. electronics production from its Texas facility.

name: Safe-T-Cap Manufacturing
old_description: Auto Rust has been reconstructing rusted cars and trucks since it was founded in 1977 by Jerry Carlson. With a background in engineering, and hailing from the manufacturing mecca of Detroit, Michigan, Jerry wanted to be in business manufacturing products for the automotive industry. One day a friend asked Jerry if he knew anyone that could weld up his old Volkswagen Beetle. Not being someone to pass up a chance to make some cash, Jerry took it into his fabrication shop and started welding - 40 years later Jerry and his team have repaired over 15,000 vehicles. Auto Rust's line of SafeTCap
about:
Safe-T-Cap Manufacturing, operating as Auto Rust Technicians, is based in Cranston, Rhode Island, in a 10,000-square-foot facility on the outskirts of Providence. The company was founded in 1977 by Jerry Carlson, an engineer from Detroit, Michigan, who began by welding a friend’s Volkswagen Beetle in his fabrication shop. Over four decades, the team has repaired more than 15,000 vehicles.

The business runs two parallel operations: a service center that restores rusted frames through sandblasting, cutting out corroded sections, and welding in proprietary Safe-T-Cap repair kits; and a manufacturing line that produces those kits. Each kit is built from American-made cold-rolled steel, assembled and welded by certified welders, and designed for installation by qualified technicians worldwide. The product range covers frame sections for Jeep Wrangler, Ford Ranger, F-150, Chevrolet/GMC Silverado and Sierra, Toyota Tacoma, 4Runner, Tundra, and FJ Cruiser, as well as Mopar, Saab, and other models.

Customers include individual vehicle owners, off-road enthusiasts, and repair shops seeking cost-effective structural repairs. The kits are sold internationally via FedEx and USPS, with online sales to the U.S. and Canada. The company’s expertise spans automotive restoration, off-road vehicles, trucks, SUVs, and classic cars.

The Safe-T-Cap line originated as internal tooling for Auto Rust’s own repairs and evolved into a DIY product line to “fix the car without being there.” The company emphasizes domestic materials, over 40 years of research and development, and a specialization it calls “rustorations,” guaranteeing its work while leaving finish bodywork and painting to other specialists.

name: Safer Textiles
old_description: Founded in 1975, Safer Textiles is a leading player within the textile industry. The company has a track record of innovation through the introduction of new processes and finishes, as well as investments in cutting edge technology.
about:
Safer Textiles was founded in 1975 by Albert Safer in Newark, New Jersey. The privately owned company operates a 180,000-square-foot facility on 5.7 acres in an Urban Enterprise Zone and employs over 125 people.

The mill is vertically integrated, handling knitting, dyeing, finishing, and coating under one roof. Its knitting department produces interlocks, jacquards, jerseys, piques, pontes, and specialty knits from a wide range of yarns. The dye house runs 25-plus modern computer-controlled machines — jets, soft flows, jigs, and atmospheric beams — with lot capacities up to 4,000 pounds and a Datacolor 800 spectrophotometer for color consistency. Finishing includes preparation (desizing, bleaching, scouring), surface treatments (napping, sueding, sanding), and chemical finishes such as flame retardant, moisture management, antimicrobial, and durable water/oil repellent. Coating uses a knife-blade process to apply water-based polyurethane on a 90-foot, 10-zone thermal range.

Safer Textiles serves apparel, medical PPE (masks, gowns meeting Levels 1–3), team sports (antimicrobial, wicking, UV-treated uniforms), military (DOD-spec fabrics), industrial (coated nylon for water/oil repellency), home furnishings, and novelty markets.

The company emphasizes turnaround times, the ability to execute high-volume orders, and a fully stocked warehouse with its own trucking network and global carriers to deliver on time. Its integrated model allows a fabric to move from raw yarn to finished product without leaving the facility, supported by ongoing R&D investment.

name: Safety Components an Elevate Textiles Company
old_description: "Since 2018, we have used Safety Components fabrics in our turnout gear, driven by the performance and durability of their outer shell and comfort of the Glide Ice liner. Our commitment to them is rooted in the enhanced safety, comfort, and wearability their materials provide. We are proud to partner with them (through our gear manufacturer) to help protect the men and women of the Indianapolis Fire Department. Safety Components' dedication to innovation, safety, service, and product education has been invaluable to us.
about:
Safety Components operates from a 22-acre campus in Greenville, South Carolina, where it has produced technical textiles since 1912. Now a subsidiary of Elevate Textiles, the company traces its roots to over a century of textile expertise in the region.

The 800,000-square-foot facility integrates weaving, coating, finishing, testing, and warehousing under one roof. Skilled associates manufacture a range of industrial fabrics — from flame-resistant outer shells and thermal liners for turnout gear to military-spec technical textiles and WeatherMAX® outdoor and marine fabrics — using substrates such as woven polyesters, nylons, and aramid fibers.

The company supplies the largest fire departments in the United States and worldwide, including the Indianapolis Fire Department, and provides materials to gear manufacturers Lion Apparel, Globe, and Honeywell. Its fabrics also serve military programs, high-performance outdoor brands, and the coating industry.

Safety Components differentiates itself through patented technologies such as Filament Twill Technology™ (2012), which yields lighter, stronger fabrics, and PF Zero™, the first commercially available PFAS-free durable water repellent finish for PPE meeting NFPA 1971. The firm also pursues sustainability targets: 100 percent renewable energy and a 40 percent water-use reduction by 2030.

name: Safety Fresh Foods
old_description: HPP is a unique, non-thermal process that kills pathogenic bacteria  (listeria, salmonella, E. coli ) and spoilage organisms (yeast, mold) through high-pressure, water-based technology. It is a USDA/FSIS and FDA-approved, 100% natural process, and is allowed for use on organic and natural products.  It uses pure cold water, and up to 87,000 psi (6,000 bar) to inactivate pathogens and dramatically extend shelf life. No chemicals. No heat. No additives.
about:
Safety Fresh Foods operates from Glendale, Wisconsin, with a high-pressure processing (HPP) facility in Plymouth, Wisconsin. The company installed a state-of-the-art HPP machine to provide non-thermal pasteurization services to food manufacturers.

The company specializes in high-pressure processing, a cold-water technology that applies up to 87,000 psi to packaged foods for a few seconds to several minutes. The process inactivates pathogens such as Listeria, Salmonella, and E. coli without heat, chemicals, or additives, preserving taste, texture, and nutrients. Shelf life typically increases three to ten times compared to untreated products stored at the same temperature. The equipment also supports cheese ripening control, meat tenderization, and flavor infusion.

Safety Fresh Foods serves food and beverage manufacturers, including dairy, meat, and beverage producers, particularly in Wisconsin. The company works with clients on innovation, cost savings, food safety, shelf-life extension, and process improvements. Its HPP service is used for organic and natural products, as well as conventional items, and is approved by USDA/FSIS and the FDA.

The company emphasizes that its non-thermal method eliminates pathogens to prevent recalls, reduces food waste, and enables clean-label, preservative-free products. It positions the technology as environmentally friendly and a way to improve profitability while sustaining the long-term viability of the regional food manufacturing industry.

name: Sanel Auto Parts Co
old_description: It all started in 1920 when Benjamin Sanel and Edward Sanel Sr. founded Sanel Auto Wrecking Company in Concord, NH. Their vision was to supply customers in northern New England with the highest quality car parts in the automotive repair business.
about:
Sanel Auto Parts Co. began in 1920 when Benjamin Sanel and Edward Sanel Sr. founded Sanel Auto Wrecking Company in Concord, New Hampshire. The business remained in the Sanel family and, after a 2018 partnership with NAPA Auto Parts, continues to operate independently as Sanel NAPA.

Today the company functions as a multi-location distributor of automotive parts, heavy-duty truck components, paint and body supplies, tools and equipment. It maintains over 46 stores across New Hampshire, Vermont, Maine and Massachusetts. In addition to distribution, Sanel runs a fully equipped machine shop that provides custom engine rebuilding for automotive, marine, diesel, powersports, performance and restoration applications, and it assembles hydraulic and air‑conditioning hose assemblies on site.

The customer base spans professional mechanics, independent service garages, individual vehicle owners, body shops, collision centers, dealerships, fleets and industrial accounts. The machine shop serves niche markets such as marine, diesel and powersports, while the body‑shop division supplies refinishing products from Axalta and 3M to collision centers and dealerships throughout the region.

It differentiates itself through a knowledgeable, professionally trained staff, convenient community locations, and specialized capabilities such as the Axalta Acquire Plus EFX color‑matching system, the Axalta VINdicator technology, and a dedicated Sanel Refinish Training Center designed to improve body‑shop productivity.

old_description: 三花汽零是全球领先的汽车领域冷热转换和温度控制相关产品和技术提供商。我们专注于新能源汽车热管理，以热泵系统、控制阀组件、换热技术和变频器控制为核心，实现了汽车热管理核心部件的全面覆盖。公司现有产品包括热力膨胀阀、单向阀、电子膨胀阀、冷媒电磁阀、电子水阀等阀类产品；电子水泵、电子油泵等泵类产品；换热器、电池冷板、贮液器、气液分离器等各系列产品。可满足新能源汽车的空调热管理、动力电池热管理、电机热管理等多种场景需求。公司已成为新能源汽车热管理领域的领军企业，自主研发的电子膨胀阀产品在2017年荣获国际创新大奖——PACE奖，是中国首家获此殊荣的民营企业。公司持续深耕汽车热管理零部件的创新研发，积极布局新能源汽车领域所需的各种热管理集成组件，为全球客户提供可提高车辆经济性、增加续航里程的产品解决方案。
about:
Sanhua Automotive USA, INC is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, serving as the North American arm of a global thermal-management specialist founded in 2004. The parent company, Zhejiang Sanhua Automotive Parts Co., Ltd., is a subsidiary of the publicly listed Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls (stock code 002050) and began as a developer of automotive thermal valves in Hangzhou, China. The U.S. entity was established to support the company's expanding North American R&D center and customer base.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of thermal-management components for new-energy vehicles, including electronic expansion valves, solenoid valves, electronic water and oil pumps, heat exchangers, battery cold plates, liquid receivers, and gas-liquid separators. Its core technologies span heat-pump systems, control-valve assemblies, heat-exchange engineering, and variable-frequency control. Globally, the organization employs over 9,600 people, with more than 1,000 dedicated to research and development across four technical centers in China, North America, and Europe, and operates five production bases in China, Mexico, Europe, and India.

Sanhua supplies major automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers in the electric-vehicle and traditional automotive sectors. Its customer roster includes Huawei, Tesla, Changan, Great Wall, BYD, Geely, SAIC, and European brands such as Volkswagen and Renault, as evidenced by numerous supplier awards from these companies. The components serve cabin climate control, battery thermal management, and electric-motor cooling applications.

The company differentiates itself through its early focus on electronic expansion valves, which earned the 2017 Automotive News PACE Award — the first such honor for a Chinese private enterprise. It emphasizes integrated thermal-management solutions that improve vehicle efficiency and extend driving range, backed by national-level engineering centers, comprehensive testing capabilities, and a portfolio of over 740 patents.

about:
Sapona Plastics LLC, headquartered in Asheboro, North Carolina, was founded in April 2004 by Jack C. Lail. The company remains privately owned by the Lail family and began with ten injection molding machines near Seagrove, NC.

Core processes include thermoplastic injection molding, insert molding, over‑molding, brush making, decorating, and assembly, supplemented by secondary operations such as hot stamping, pad printing, ultrasonic welding, fusion welding, machining, labeling, spin welding, hot‑melt gluing, foam filling, brush bristling, and heat staking. The company also provides part and mold design project management, in‑house CAD, on‑site tool maintenance, warehousing, fulfillment, and distribution, producing millions of parts and assemblies each week with annual sales exceeding $20 million.

Sapona serves the personal care, consumer goods, telecommunications, electrical, industrial, HVAC, medical, automotive, agricultural, and lighting markets. Typical products include buckets, brushes, scrubbers, fiber‑optic and cable components, filter components, electrical and lighting enclosures, control and cable enclosures, and sporting goods.

The company emphasizes a “Fast, Reliable and Cost Effective” strategy: on‑time delivery with proactive communication, early design‑for‑manufacture involvement, RJG‑certified Master Molders, cGMP‑ and ISO‑compliant quality systems, 24‑hour operation, and all‑electric presses that run up to 25% more efficiently. Recycling and post‑consumer recycled material options are also offered.

about:
Schmersal Inc., headquartered in Hawthorne, New York, is the U.S. arm of the Schmersal Group, a family-owned enterprise founded in 1945 in Germany. The company operates as an owner-managed Mittelstand firm with global reach, producing safety switching devices and systems for machine guarding and occupational safety.

The company manufactures a broad portfolio of safety-related switchgear and control components, including safety switches with separate actuators, safety interlocks, non-contact safety sensors (light curtains, grids, and barriers), safety relay modules, programmable safety controllers, and ATEX-certified explosion-proof switches. It also supplies elevator technology components and offers the tec.nicum service division for manufacturer-neutral safety consulting, training, and lean production support. Global headcount exceeds 1,000 employees.

Schmersal serves machine builders, system integrators, and plant operators across industrial automation, general manufacturing, material handling, factory automation, and explosion-hazard environments. Its safety systems are deployed in applications ranging from guard-door monitoring and emergency-stop circuits to complex safety-related control architectures for automated production lines and elevators.

The firm emphasizes its “complete solutions from a single source” approach—combining components, control systems, and software into tailored safety concepts—and cites the flexibility of a family-owned mid-sized company paired with the international presence of a corporation as a key differentiator. It also claims to offer the world’s largest range of safety switches and safety systems.
